meta.title: Kanji Write: Kanji Stroke Order and Writing Practice
meta.description: Learn to write kanji, hiragana and katakana by hand on iPhone and iPad. Every stroke is checked for shape, position, direction and order. Free.
meta.ogTitle: Kanji Write: every stroke is checked
meta.ogDescription: Write kanji and kana with a finger or Apple Pencil. The app checks the shape, position, direction and order of each stroke.
meta.ogImageAlt: The kanji 学 written stroke by stroke next to the words Kanji Write

store.requirement: iPhone and iPad, iOS 16 or later

hero.title: Learn kanji stroke order by hand
hero.lede: Write each character with a finger or Apple Pencil. Kanji Write checks every stroke as you draw it and tells you what to fix.
hero.demoLabel: Stroke order of the kanji 学, drawn one stroke at a time
hero.screenAlt: Kanji Write Home screen on iPhone with JLPT level filters, the Practice group with New, Review and Words, and a grid of N5 kanji

checks.title: Four checks on every stroke
checks.lede: Kanji Write compares each line you draw with the reference stroke. It accepts the stroke only when all four checks pass.

items.title: Shape
items.body: Your line must follow the shape of the stroke, hooks and turns included.

items.title: Position
items.body: The stroke must sit in the right part of the square, so the character keeps its balance.

items.title: Direction
items.body: A stroke drawn from the wrong end is rejected, even when it looks right.

items.title: Order
items.body: Strokes count only in the correct order, in every practice mode.

checks.feedbackTitle: It tells you what went wrong
checks.feedbackBody: A rejected stroke comes with a reason: right shape but wrong order, wrong shape, or too far from where the stroke belongs. You fix that one stroke and continue.
messages: Right shape, wrong order: that was stroke 3. Draw stroke 1 first.
The shape doesn't match this stroke.
Too far from where this stroke belongs.

try.title: Write a kanji in your browser
try.lede: Draw the strokes in order with a mouse, a finger or a pen. The demo uses the app's stroke data and a simpler version of its check.
try.wrongOrder: Right shape, wrong order. Draw stroke {current} first.
try.wrongDirection: Wrong direction. Start from the other end.
try.wrongShape: The shape does not match this stroke.
try.done: Complete. All {total} strokes are in order.
try.noScript: This demo needs JavaScript. The app does not.

guides.title: From tracing to writing on your own
guides.lede: Choose how much help you get. The app remembers your choice and checks stroke order at every level.

items.name: Trace
items.title: Write over the whole character
items.body: The full character shows as a guide. You draw over it, and each stroke is checked.
items.screenAlt: Trace mode on iPhone: the kanji 学 as a light guide, with the first strokes written over it

items.name: Guided
items.title: See only the next stroke
items.body: The guide shows one stroke at a time, so you learn the order step by step.
items.screenAlt: Guided mode on iPhone: the kanji 書 almost complete, with only the next stroke shown as a guide

items.name: Copy
items.title: Write with no guide
items.body: The square is empty. The character stays in view above it, and you copy it.
items.screenAlt: Copy mode on iPhone: the kanji 学 written by hand in an empty grid, with the model character above it

practice.title: Learn new characters, then review them from memory
practice.lede: The Home screen has one Practice group with two buttons, so you always know where to start.

items.name: New
items.title: Characters you have not written yet
items.body: New starts a session of characters you have not practised, at the guide level you chose.
items.screenAlt: Home screen on iPhone with the New and Review buttons in the Practice group

items.name: Review
items.title: Write from memory
items.body: Review hides the character and shows only its readings and meaning. When you are stuck, a hint shows the character or the next stroke.
items.screenAlt: Review session on iPhone: the character is hidden behind a question mark, and its meaning and readings are shown

points: Characters that needed a hint or a retry come first in Review.
The Review button shows how many characters are waiting.
The Progress screen shows your practice days, completed characters and the last five weeks.
practice.progressAlt: Progress screen on iPhone with the number of days, completions and characters, a calendar of the last month and a list of characters to review

sentences.title: Write whole words and sentences
sentences.lede: On iPad you write a full sentence, one square for each character. On iPhone, the Words practice gives you whole words.
points: Each sentence comes with its reading and an English translation.
Three modes: Free to write over the characters with no check, Trace to write over them with every stroke checked, Empty to write them in blank squares.
You can play the reading aloud.
sentences.screenAlt: Sentence writing on iPad in Empty mode: a row of squares with handwritten characters, the next square active, and the reading and English translation above

ipad.title: Made for Apple Pencil
ipad.lede: On iPad the writing area gets the whole screen. With Apple Pencil, practice feels like writing in a paper notebook.

items.title: Apple Pencil
items.body: Write with Apple Pencil or a finger on iPad, and with a finger on iPhone.

items.title: Haptic feedback
items.body: Apple Pencil Pro gives a light tap when you complete a character or a sentence. On iPhone, the phone itself gives the feedback.

items.title: Notebook
items.body: Pick a character and fill rows of squares, as on squared paper. The model stays at the start of each row.

items.title: Sidebar layout
items.body: The sidebar holds search, filters and the character list. It hides on writing screens, so the canvas gets the full width.

ipad.homeAlt: Kanji Write on iPad: the sidebar with search, filters, the Practice group and the kanji grid, and the selected kanji 学 with Practice and Notebook buttons
ipad.notebookAlt: Notebook on iPad: the kanji 学 as a model at the start of each row, followed by handwritten copies

library.title: 2,200+ kanji and all the kana
library.lede: Filter by JLPT level, by Japanese school grade or by kana. Search by character, reading or English meaning, and play readings aloud.

stats.label: hiragana and katakana, with voiced forms and yōon

library.glyphsLabel: Examples of kanji and kana from the app, drawn in stroke order

more.title: Small things that help you practise every day

items.title: Works offline
items.body: All character data is in the app. It needs no internet connection.

items.title: No account, no tracking
items.body: There is no sign-up, no analytics and no advertising.

items.title: iCloud sync
items.body: Practice history syncs between your own devices through your private iCloud.

items.title: Daily kanji widget
items.body: A widget shows one kanji each day on the Home Screen or Lock Screen. Tap it to start practice.

items.title: Strictness
items.body: Choose how closely strokes must match: normal or strict. Strict also checks stroke length.

items.title: Your ink
items.body: Change the ink colour, the guide colours and the guide width.

items.q: How does Kanji Write check stroke order?
items.a: Kanji Write compares each stroke you draw with a reference stroke from KanjiVG. It checks the shape, the position, the direction and the place of the stroke in the order. If a check fails, the stroke is rejected and the app tells you why.
Yes. Kanji Write is free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, with no in-app purchases and no ads.
More than 2,200 kanji: JLPT N5 to N1, the kanji of Japanese elementary school grades 1 to 6 and the other jōyō kanji. Also all hiragana and katakana, with voiced forms and yōon combinations.

items.q: Can I write kanji with Apple Pencil?
items.a: Yes. On iPad you can write with Apple Pencil, and Apple Pencil Pro gives haptic feedback. You can also write with a finger on iPhone and iPad.
Yes. All character data is in the app, so it works with no internet connection. There is no account, and the app collects no data.

items.q: Is Kanji Write good for JLPT kanji study?
items.a: Yes. You can filter kanji by JLPT level from N5 to N1 and practise one level at a time. Writing each kanji by hand, stroke by stroke, helps you remember its form and its stroke order.

items.q: What is the difference between New and Review?
items.a: New gives you characters that you have not practised yet, with a guide. Review hides the character, and you write it from memory from its readings and meaning. Characters that needed a hint or a retry come first.

items.q: Which languages does Kanji Write support?
items.a: The app interface is in English and Japanese. Kanji meanings and sentence translations are in English.
Not yet. An Android version is in development, with no release date. Kanji Write is available now for iPhone and iPad.
